Research

How can we make virtual objects feel real? My research builds haptic interfaces that render force, weight, and texture — combining perceptual science with wearable hardware.

Theme 01

Chemical Haptics

Using chemical substances to evoke thermal and tactile sensations. I induce the thermal grill illusion — a burning sensation from interleaved warm and cold — chemically rather than with thermal devices, and present popping sensations from sprays, linking stimulus design to perception through psychophysics.

7 papers ↗
figure
Theme 02

Electrical Stimulation

Making electro-tactile displays comfortable and expressive. By applying anesthetic cream I suppress the itch and pain of electrical stimulation and widen its usable dynamic range, enabling stronger and clearer pressure and vibration cues.

2 papers ↗
figure
Theme 03

Thermal & Cooling Feedback

Wearable devices that deliver warmth and cold in everyday settings. ALCool harnesses alcohol's evaporative cooling for ubiquitous cold feedback, and Enchanted Touch layers thermal and vibrotactile cues onto real objects without covering the fingerpad.

2 papers ↗
